technical_and_design_decisions: User story U5 is a duplicate of U4; both will be fulfilled by a single unified module storage implementation in HDFS.
The ACL user story (U2) is treated purely as a spike deliverable (design specification, DSL/UI scope identification, and next steps documentation) rather than production code implementation.
The CPU startup profiling activity (U3) focuses on diagnosis, bottleneck identification, and architectural recommendations rather than implementing performance refactoring code.
HDFS and YARN configuration overrides (U6, U7) will be exposed via externalized environment variables and Spring configuration properties tailored for Cloud Foundry deployments.
Spark job cancellation (U8) will leverage the native Spark/YARN client APIs to programmatically signal job termination and trigger cleanup handlers.
assumptions: Development, build pipeline, and integration test environments with access to Hadoop HDFS, YARN, and Spark clusters are already set up and accessible.
The single developer has requisite expertise in Spring XD framework internals, Java profiling tools (e.g., JProfiler/async-profiler), and Hadoop ecosystem integration.
Standard enterprise security tools and Java 17+ compatibility apply to all module components.

activities.activity_description: Design and build a flexible RxJava processor module to support reactive stream processing, including unit tests and standard module descriptor bindings.
Review customer access control use cases, evaluate XD runtime constraints, define DSL/UI scope, and draft complete ACL design specifications.
Profile startup sequences for admin and container servers using Java profiling tools, isolate CPU performance bottlenecks, and document pros/cons of proposed optimizations.
Implement high-availability storage and retrieval mechanism for custom module uber-jars in HDFS to support failover and reinstall scenarios.

activities.activity_name: Cloud Foundry HDFS & YARN Location Overrides
activities.activity_description: Implement configurable overrides for HDFS module storage paths and YARN configuration locations targeting Cloud Foundry deployment environments.
Implement functionality to stop running Spark jobs on demand and verify prompt release of cluster resources upon job completion or cancellation.
Perform full integration testing across all implemented features, verify CF and HDFS configuration flows, and update developer documentation.
